title: Week 3 Capacity Check-In
subtitle: Connect your daily choices to the activities that matter to you.
description: Recovery is not a test of perfect habits or perfect thinking. This check-in helps identify one useful action and the evidence it gives you.

sections.title: Notice capacity
sections.description: Progress can show up in more places than symptom intensity.

fields.label: Where did you notice evidence of progress?
options: I completed more of a meaningful activity
I recovered more predictably after activity
I felt more confident trying something
I changed position or adjusted a task without panic
I responded differently to a difficult thought
I supported my energy with food, sleep, hydration, or recovery time
I asked for useful support or clarification

fields.label: Describe one specific example.
fields.placeholder: What did you do, and what did it show you?

sections.title: Test a prediction
sections.description: Use a CBT-style experiment without dismissing real symptoms or safety concerns.

fields.label: A difficult prediction I noticed:
fields.placeholder: For example: If I do this, I will be unable to cope afterward...

fields.label: A more balanced statement:
fields.placeholder: Accurate, realistic, and not falsely positive...

fields.label: What manageable action could help test that prediction?
fields.placeholder: Choose an appropriate step and what you will observe...

sections.title: Act on what matters
sections.description: Choose a meaningful direction, then scale the action to your current capacity.

fields.label: One activity, role, or value that matters to me:
fields.placeholder: Connection, work, parenting, recreation, independence, health...

fields.label: One small action I will take toward it:
What support or adjustment would make this easier?
fields.placeholder: A smaller starting point, task modification, clearer plan, or conversation with your practitioner...

successMessage: Week 3 complete. You are using recovery skills to build capacity in the parts of life that matter.
